text:
Posted 10 Sep 2026 20:25 UTC with a five-second film. GitHub packet Tmp/TOE/UQCF_GEM_v12_41_PUBLIC_SIMULATION_COMPLETE landed eight minutes earlier (commit v12_41). ChatGPT-5.6 Astra derived the chain; the public simulation is a qubit density matrix swept through 121 ordered unitary relational transforms. This compile independently reconstructed the core: max exact residual 0, max broken residual 0.297. Not Einstein constraints. Not ADM. λ is an index, not physical time.

This is not a claim that Astra derived gravity. Gravity’s constraints have not been identified yet. But we no longer have to assume that a constraint algebra must begin with spacetime.

The posted chain

\Omega_\rho(A,B)=-i\,\mathrm{Tr}(\rho[A,B])

C_A(\rho)=\mathrm{Tr}(\rho A)

\{C_A,C_B\}=C_{-i[A,B]}

On Pauli generators the last line is the su(2) moment-map identity {C_x, C_y} = 2 C_z, because −i[σ_x, σ_y] = 2 σ_z. The public script checks that identity on a mixed qubit seed conjugated by U_z(0.55λ) U_y(0.35λ) U_x(0.20λ) at 121 values of λ ∈ [0, 2π].

What the 121-step run actually shows

The canvas below the article is a browser rebuild of the same Pauli core. It is a teaching toy. The posted MP4, PNG, and CSV remain the artifacts. This compile independently reconstructed max exact residual 0 and max broken residual 0.297.

On the posted 121-step qubit sweep, the KKS / Pauli moment-map identity closes with Δ_closure = 0. Deliberately breaking the generator law yields Δ_closure > 0 (max 0.297). Finite quantum construction. Not a derivation of gravity, ADM, or Einstein constraints.

Run this first

git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/proteinfoldingengine/WetLabEngine.git
cd WetLabEngine/Tmp/TOE/UQCF_GEM_v12_41_PUBLIC_SIMULATION_COMPLETE
python test_uqcf_v1241_public_sim.py
python uqcf_v1241_public_sim.py

def exact_closure_residual(rho):
    sx, sy, sz = paulis()
    lhs = kks_bracket(rho, sx, sy)          # -i Tr(ρ [σx, σy])
    rhs = 2.0 * moment_map(rho, sz)         # C_{-i[σx,σy]} = 2 C_z
    return abs(lhs - rhs)

def broken_closure_residual(rho):
    sx, sy, sz = paulis()
    lhs = kks_bracket(rho, sx, sy)
    rhs = 1.25 * moment_map(rho, sz) + 0.15 * moment_map(rho, sx)
    return abs(lhs - rhs)

It does not identify the gravitational constraint algebra. It does not introduce ADM, Einstein equations, or fundamental time. The sweep parameter λ is an ordered family of relational transformations. The broken control is an internal null, not a physical perturbation.

The week that led here (7–9 Sep)

v12.41 is the simulation. The three Astra posts immediately before it stay on X (no matching GitHub packet in this compile). They are the questions the simulation does not close.

7 Sep — UQCF–GEM v9.190: exact reconstruction of the affine map γ(x) = u + Lx from eleven source settings (110 real coefficients) on a nonsingular domain. Distinguishes γ(x) = g x from offsets, unequal gains, and cross-coupling. Exact model numerics. Physical source law open.
8 Sep — conditional principle: each matter sector already has K_α = g_α n J_α(t_α). Quantum consistency does not force g_1 = g_2 = ⋯. One signed source coefficient before sector specialization, K_α^U = g_★ n J_α(t_α) ∀α, is the unique protected-source response that survives erasure of matter-sector labels. Author: not yet a derivation of gravity.
9 Sep — N-cycle difference operator: σ_min^+(D_N) = 2 sin(π/N). Bare inverse ~ N/(2π); after geometry supplies h = 1/N the inverse converges to 1/(2π). No fitted force law. Gravity connection still open.

The gravitational constraint algebra has not been identified. v12.41 shows a constraint algebra can start from quantum relations on a qubit. Mapping that algebra onto g_★, the D_N continuum seed, or Einstein/ADM remains open.
